$comment: The input format of the plan §11.5 whiteboard compiler. plan §11.5 states seven section headings as prose in a code block; INV-003 makes this document — not that prose — normative for the shape, and RFC 0038 'Whiteboard compiler' records why each undecided question is decided the way it is here.

handle.$comment: The artifact-handle spelling of evidence-graph-node.schema.json's `artifact` and `provenance.inputs[]`, transcribed rather than narrowed: a handle a note names must be a handle the graph could publish.

entry.description: One line of a whiteboard section. There is deliberately no status, confidence, verdict, or assurance member: docs/44 'status words in prose do not promote status', and a field a producer can fill is a field a producer can lie in (RFC 0038 D3). Everything compiled from an entry lands at `proposed`.

claim.description: The claim identity this entry is about, as evidence-graph-node.schema.json `claim_id`. Required and explicit: status promotion is linearized per claim identity (plan §11.7), and a claim identity derived from the entry's wording would make 'is this the same claim the graph already holds?' a function of phrasing.

references.description: Prior artifacts this entry is derived from. docs/44 'references must resolve': the compiler refuses the whole note when the graph holds no node about one of these. They become the compiled node's `provenance.inputs` — derivation, never assertion.

subject.description: The artifact this entry is about, which becomes the compiled node's `artifact`. Deliberately NOT required to resolve in the graph: an entry whose subject the graph already held could propose nothing new, and proposing is what a whiteboard is for.

text.description: The human sentence. Carried beside the compiled node and never inside it — INV-003: 'human text may accompany a machine result, never define it'. The compiler never parses it, so no wording in it can reach the graph.

decision.description: A plan §11.5 `Decision` entry. docs/44 'conclusions require supporting edges', so `references` is non-empty here and only here, and each reference becomes a SUPPORTS edge into the compiled decision node.

references.description: At least one supporting artifact. An empty list is what docs/44 forbids: a conclusion with no supporting edge.

experiment.description: A plan §11.5 `Experiment` entry. docs/44 'experiments become task proposals', and plan §11.2's twenty node kinds have no task kind, so an experiment compiles to a task proposal rather than to a node — which is why it carries neither `claim` nor `subject`.

references.description: Prior artifacts the experiment would be run against. Held to the same 'references must resolve' rule as an entry's.

author.description: Who wrote the note, in evidence-graph-node.schema.json's actor vocabulary (RFC 0038 'Authority'). Pinned to the four schemes here rather than left an open string, because RFC 0038 D3's rule that an agent/human/ci actor may not appear as a checker requires the scheme to be readable from the bytes. Every scheme may author a note: everything a note compiles to is `proposed`, which docs/44 gives to 'any authorized human/agent'.

counterexamples.description: plan §11.5 `Counterexample`. Compiles to `counterexample` nodes (plan §11.2). No REFUTES or COUNTEREXAMPLE_TO edge is emitted: whether a counterexample actually refutes a candidate is a semantic judgement the compiler cannot make, and asserting it from a section heading would be the empty-success shape the dossier rejects.

created_at.description: When the note was written. Becomes every compiled node's `provenance.created_at`, so the compiler reads no clock (INV-005, ADR-0003). `format` and nothing more, exactly as evidence-graph-node.schema.json spells `provenance.created_at`; the canonical byte spelling is the daemon's Timestamp scalar and this document does not invent a third one.

decisions.description: plan §11.5 `Decision`. Compiles to `decision` nodes (plan §11.2 `ReviewDecision`) plus the SUPPORTS edges docs/44 requires of a conclusion.

experiments.description: plan §11.5 `Experiment`. Compiles to task proposals, not to nodes.

goal.description: plan §11.5 `Goal`. Exactly one, and required: §11.5 opens 'for complex invention tasks', singular, and a note with two goals is two notes. Compiles to a `property` node — plan §11.2 `Property` is 'a property to be established', which is what a whiteboard goal is; `proof_goal` is reserved for the obligations below, which are what a proof worker is handed.

known_facts.description: plan §11.5 `Known facts`. Compiles to `assumption` nodes (plan §11.2): what an author knows is, to the graph, what the author's claims are conditional on. Reading it as `observed` evidence would be exactly the promotion docs/44 forbids prose from performing.

allOf.$comment: A whiteboard note is provisional (docs/44) and is deliberately not one of plan §4.4's content-addressed artifact classes, so it mints no new class prefix; the generic handle spelling is the one intent-registry-record.record_id and synthesis-candidate.candidate_id already use. The two exclusions are the classes it must not be able to impersonate: `ev_` names an evidence node or edge, and this note appears in `provenance.inputs` where an `ev_` handle would read as graph content; `cap_` tokens confer authority, and a note confers none.

note_id.description: The handle whoever holds the note names it by. It is an input, not an authority: it appears in every compiled node's `provenance.inputs` so the derivation is recorded, and nothing else.

schema_epoch.description: Schema epoch this instance was written against (schemas/README.md). It advances only on a breaking change to this artifact class, is not one of the six independently versioned epochs (RFC 0026 `rule versioning.epoch_independence`), and pins no semantics.

schema_id.description: Artifact-class identity of the governing schema: its `$id` with the `v<schema_epoch>/` segment removed (schemas/README.md). Stable across schema epochs.

tool.description: The tool or model version that produced the note (docs/44 'Credit and provenance': actor/tool/model version). Optional, and the one member of the note that is optional rather than empty-able: `provenance.tool` is itself present exactly when a tool was named.

unresolved_obligations.description: plan §11.5 `Unresolved obligation`. Compiles to `proof_goal` nodes (plan §11.2 `ProofGoal`, 'a goal handed to a proof worker'), which is what an unresolved obligation is.

title: Whiteboard Note
